# COR003 `implicit-external-procedures`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="info" text="opt-in" />

`implicit none` does not forbid implicit external procedures (`implicit none (type, external)`).

## Why

Plain `implicit none` still lets a call to an unknown name compile as a reference to an external
procedure with an implicit interface: a misspelled procedure name surfaces only at link time, and
argument mismatches never. Fortran 2018 `implicit none (type, external)` turns both into compile
errors.

## Reported

```fortran
implicit none
```

## Preferred

```fortran
implicit none (type, external)
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[COR003] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = COR003` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `C003` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
